title: FlashGNN: An In-SSD Accelerator for GNN Training
problem: Single-machine GNN training is bottlenecked by slow PCIe data transfer and flash memory access latency, resulting in low CPU and GPU utilization.
motivation: Real-world graph datasets exceed centralized system capabilities, and distributed systems suffer from network bandwidth limitations.
method: FlashGNN designs SSD firmware to coordinate data movements and hardware access, utilizing I/O parallelism in flash chips while maximizing data reuse. It employs a node-wise GNN training method, an efficient flash request scheduling algorithm, and high-performance subgraph generation optimized for flash memory constraints.
key_novelty: In-SSD accelerator architecture that uses firmware-level coordination to overcome PCIe bottlenecks and exploit flash chip I/O parallelism for GNN training.
contributions: In-SSD accelerator design with firmware coordination for data movements and hardware access
Node-wise GNN training method optimized for flash memory access patterns
Efficient flash request scheduling algorithm for I/O parallelism utilization
High-performance subgraph generation method for flash-based GNN processing
